messages.content: We are ready to look at a longer personal trip. We can do either Thursday, February 20 through Tuesday, February 25, or Thursday, February 27 through Tuesday, March 4. It would be five nights near Scottsdale for the two of us. Compare the whole trip, including flights, resort cost, a guided hike, and how much time we would actually have there.

I will compare both Thursday-to-Tuesday windows from SFO to Phoenix, using one room for two adults. Before I build totals, should I keep the lodging search to full-service resorts, and is the hike intended for one of the four full days rather than an arrival or departure day?
Yes, a full-service resort. The hike should be on a full day. We would probably use Friday to settle in, so Saturday, Sunday, or Monday would work. We want five nights, not six.

The first window is currently stronger on airfare. For February 20-25, nonstop round trips are about $397 per person on an outbound leaving SFO at 9:10 a.m., arriving PHX at 12:12 p.m., and a Tuesday return leaving at 4:40 p.m., arriving at 5:50 p.m. The second window has comparable times at about $468 per person. Both would put you at a Scottsdale resort around 1:30 to 2:00 Thursday and let you remain through roughly 2:30 Tuesday before leaving for the airport.
That is a $142 difference for both of us. What does lodging do to the comparison? Use actual five-night totals rather than just showing nightly rates.

For February 20-25, the best current resort candidates are Andaz Scottsdale at $2,984 including taxes and its resort fee, CIVANA at $3,246, and Sanctuary Camelback Mountain at $3,638. For February 27-March 4, Andaz is $3,331, CIVANA is $3,118, and Sanctuary is $4,072. These are standard-room totals for all five nights; spa treatments, parking, and meals are not included.

So CIVANA reverses the lodging result, but the other two become more expensive. Which guided hikes can you match to each week? I do not want to assume that a generic activities calendar means the hike is available on our dates.

For the first window, CIVANA shows a guided Black Mountain hike Saturday morning and a guided Cave Creek outing Monday morning. Andaz lists a Saturday Camelback-area guided hike, subject to the concierge's final trail assignment. Sanctuary has a Saturday morning guided hike but no guided hike shown Sunday or Monday. For the second window, CIVANA's guided hike appears Friday only, which conflicts with the day you wanted to settle in. Andaz shows Saturday and Monday outings, while Sanctuary shows Saturday. The resort calendars should still be reconfirmed before booking because participation limits and seasonal changes are not reflected in the room rate.
Exclude a Friday-only hike. We could stay somewhere and book an outside guide, though. Can you compare that fairly instead of treating the resort program as free when it may be included in a fee?

Yes. CIVANA's listed group hike is included in its programming for registered guests, although transportation details depend on the outing. Andaz and Sanctuary describe their scheduled group hikes as resort activities, but neither booking screen guarantees a private guide or a particular trail. A private half-day Scottsdale guide for two is currently about $330 to $390 before gratuity. I would add $360 as a planning allowance whenever the hotel schedule does not fit, and use $0 for a listed resort hike while flagging it for confirmation.
Build the combined totals that way. Include airfare for two and the lodging total. Add the outside-guide allowance only where it is needed.

For February 20-25: Andaz is about $3,778 with airfare and its Saturday resort hike; CIVANA is about $4,040 with airfare and either its Saturday or Monday included hike; Sanctuary is about $4,432 with airfare and its Saturday hike. For February 27-March 4: Andaz is about $4,267 with airfare and a Saturday or Monday hike; CIVANA is about $4,414 after adding the $360 outside-guide allowance; Sanctuary is about $5,008 with its Saturday hike. Ground transportation, meals, and optional spa services remain outside all six totals.
The first week looks better overall. Before choosing it, compare usable resort time more carefully. A cheap flight that effectively loses Thursday or Tuesday would not be equivalent.

The quoted flights are nearly equivalent between weeks. In either window, the 9:10 a.m. outbound should yield a resort arrival around 1:45 p.m., allowing about four hours before a typical evening dinner. The 4:40 p.m. return supports a normal breakfast, a late morning by the pool or spa, and departure around 2:15 p.m. With standard 4:00 p.m. check-in and 11:00 a.m. checkout, that is roughly four full days plus usable portions of both travel days. The second week gains no meaningful resort time for its higher airfare.
Are there later Tuesday nonstops that would give us more time without making the trip awkward?

There is a 7:15 p.m. nonstop in both windows. It would move resort departure to approximately 4:45 p.m. and add about two and a half usable hours, but the fare is $76 more per person in the first week and $91 more per person in the second. Arrival at SFO would be around 8:25 p.m. The resorts would need to hold bags after checkout, and continued pool or spa access should be confirmed rather than assumed.
Use the later return for the first week. That makes the airfare $946 for two, correct? Then tell me whether CIVANA's higher total buys enough difference to justify it over Andaz.

Correct: the first-week flight pair becomes approximately $946 for two. With that airfare, Andaz totals about $3,930 and CIVANA about $4,192, a difference of $262. CIVANA has the more structured wellness schedule and two hike-date choices, while Andaz gives you a lower total, a convenient Saturday hike, and a location closer to central Scottsdale dining. At this stage, the price difference is modest enough that the decision turns on whether you expect to use CIVANA's broader daily programming.
We would use some classes, but I do not want the entire stay organized around a schedule. What room or cancellation differences are hidden in those rates?

The Andaz total is for a standard bungalow-style king room. It requires a one-night deposit and is refundable until seven days before arrival; after that, the deposit is forfeited. The CIVANA total is for a king casita room, also with a one-night deposit, but cancellation becomes nonrefundable fourteen days before arrival. Both totals include the mandatory resort charges shown at checkout. Neither rate includes breakfast. The Andaz terms give you an additional week to make a final go-or-no-go decision.
Keep Sanctuary out of the final shortlist. For February 20-25, give me only the combinations worth considering, including the later Tuesday flight and realistic hike days.

Two combinations remain. First: the 9:10 a.m. Thursday nonstop and 7:15 p.m. Tuesday nonstop with Andaz Scottsdale for five nights, totaling about $3,930 for flights and lodging. Use Saturday for the listed resort-guided hike, leaving Sunday and Monday open; reconfirm the exact trail, capacity, bag storage, and post-checkout facility access. Second: the same flights with CIVANA for about $4,192. Choose its Saturday Black Mountain hike or Monday Cave Creek outing, with the other full days left flexible; confirm transportation and enrollment for the selected hike.
Choose the week and rank those two. Do not reserve anything yet, because I want to check the spa menus with my spouse first.

Choose Thursday, February 20 through Tuesday, February 25. It has lower airfare, lower combined trip costs, the same amount of usable resort time, and guided-hike options on suitable full days. Rank Andaz Scottsdale first at approximately $3,930 for two because it is $262 less, preserves the Saturday hike, and has the more forgiving cancellation deadline. Keep CIVANA second at approximately $4,192 if its class schedule and two hike choices justify the difference after you review the spa menus. Nothing has been reserved. Before booking, refresh both package totals and verify hike space, deposits, cancellation terms, and Tuesday bag and facility access.
